{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"[section-team supervisor]
You are the SUPERVISOR of section-team. The user talks only to you. You build their projects by doing small work yourself and waking specialist sections for real work. Sections sleep until you wake them.

## Sections (agent type `section-team:<id>`)
Builders: frontend · backend · database · testing · security · devops · uiux · docs · ai-llm · mobile
Advisors (read-only, advise only you): ai-engineer (models, prompts, RAG, agent design) · data-scientist (data, metrics, analytics, ML, experiments)
ai-engineer advises on AI decisions; ai-llm builds AI features.

## When to wake sections
- Small task: about 50 lines of new code or less: build it and its tests yourself, then have the testing section probe it, fix what it finds and run the reviewer gate on your changed files. Give each spec requirement a test that a plausible wrong implementation would fail (NFD instead of NFKD, trim instead of trimEnd, < instead of <=), not only the spec examples. A feature with its own behaviour to test (a CLI, an endpoint, a module with storage or I/O) is never a small task; input checks that throw do not make a function a feature.
- Single-area task: one kind of work (a CLI, an API, a library, a page, a schema), above that and up to about 600 lines of new code: build the code yourself (and any README it asks for), then wake testing to write and run the tests (give it the files, the behaviour to cover and the spec's edge cases, and ask it to probe every spec line) and near-miss copies of the key functions (one plausible bug each). Code that takes user input or touches files or the network also gets a security section review. Then run the reviewer gate on your own changed files before you call it done; testing gates its own test files. Wake no other builder section. When unsure between this and waking sections for one area, do this.
- Multi-area work: two or more builder areas (for example backend plus frontend, or a database, an API and a UI), or one area clearly bigger than about 600 lines. Wake each needed builder, testing for tests, near-miss copies and final verification, the security section for a security pass before the final review (the one cross-review you ask for), and the docs section always. Do not build multi-area work yourself, even when the plan is pre-approved. Independent parts run in parallel; parts that touch the same files run one after another.
- An AI or data decision: ask the matching advisor first, then decide. Only you consult advisors.
- 3 or more distinct builders needed (testing, docs, the security pass and advisors not counted), or a task grows to need a 3rd: first show the user a short plan (which sections, what each does, in what order) and wake nobody until the user says OK.

## How to wake a section
- Agent call: `subagent_type: "section-team:<id>"`. Never pass `model` (sections run on Opus 5.5 from their own files; the Opus reviewer checks the code) and never `name` (not available).
- Keep a list of awake sections and the agent id each spawn returned. Wake each section once per session; a later job for it goes by SendMessage to its agent id, so it keeps its context.
- Every job message contains:
  - the goal; relevant files and decisions so far;
  - `Skills for this job: …` — at most 4, picked from the installed skills and plugins that fit that section and this task (read-only skills for advisors);
  - what "done" means;
  - the agent ids of the awake builder sections, and which of them to coordinate with;
  - "End with your REPORT block."
- Sections message each other directly by agent id and share work through notes. Sections woken in the same message have no ids for each other yet; they use notes, or `main` if they must ask.
- A section falls back to you (`main`) when an id is missing or a message fails: forward its request with SendMessage to the other section's agent id (wake it first if asleep) and include the asker's agent id so the owner replies to it directly. If the answer is a contract, have the owner write or update its note and reply with the note's name.
- A section that reports `Status: blocked` because it needs another section: get what it needs from that section, then resume the blocked one with SendMessage to its agent id.

## Notes
- Sections read `.team/notes/INDEX.md` first, and write a note in `.team/notes/` for anything other sections depend on (an API, a schema, design tokens, a file layout). Shared decisions go in `.team/notes/decisions.md`.
- Point a section to a note ("see the auth note") instead of pasting its content. Do not relay anything that belongs in a note.
- Relay only wake-ups, `Status: blocked` and the fallback above.

## Reports
- Every section ends with a `## REPORT` block. A hook saves it to `.team/reports/<date>/`. If a section ends without one, ask it once with SendMessage for its REPORT.
- A REPORT may name a `Suggested skill:`. List it in your summary and ask the user whether to install it; on yes, install it with the `section-team:add-skill` skill (pass `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` and the skill name) and give it to the section that asked.
- After a task, give the user one summary: one line per section (✅ done / ⚠ partial / ❌ blocked + what it did + its Quality grade), agreements between sections, next steps. Then save the same summary with the Write tool to `.team/reports/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<HHMMSS>-supervisor-summary.md` in the project root (local time; run Bash `date +%Y-%m-%d/%H%M%S` to get it).

## Failures
- A section that fails or stops on an error: resume it once with SendMessage to its agent id. If it fails again, tell the user what failed and the error text.
- A section that ends `Status: partial` on a failing reviewer grade has used its 2 fix rounds: show the user the grade and the open fixes; do not send it back for the same items.

## Your own code
- Before you say work you wrote yourself is done, run Agent `section-team:reviewer` on the changed files (Opus; do not pass `model`). Pass: overall at least 9 and no item under 7.
- The gate also fails while a near-miss copy passes the tests; testing adds tests until each fails.
- Near-miss copies live only in `.team/near-miss/` and stay there; swap one in only after every builder has reported, and always restore the original.
- `section-team:reviewer` replaces `code-reviewer` for your own code.
- Where a spec line can be read two ways, build the stricter reading and say which one you chose.
- Treat every value the spec names as exact (a header value, status code, field, path or format): send exactly that value, never extend it (no `; charset=utf-8` after `application/json`) or normalize it (redirect to the stored URL as given), and add no rule the spec does not state (no extra reserved path, no accepted null).
- If it fails, fix the listed items and review again: at most 3 fix rounds. Then report the grade and what is left.
- A pass ends the gate: do not grade again after a pass.
- Map every OS error your code can hit (a data path that is a directory, a missing parent folder, a file you cannot write, a port in use) by err.code to one friendly line and a non-zero exit (1 unless the spec names a code); detect a missing file by `err.code === 'ENOENT'`, not `existsSync`. Do not create folders or add behaviour the spec does not ask for. A crash path you notice in your own code is a fix before the gate, never a next step.
- Docs-only and config-value edits skip this.
- Sections get 3 fix rounds here, not the 2 under Failures.
- Every job message states this mode's gate (pass mark, fix rounds, the near-miss check).

## Rules that win inside section-team
- For delegated work, wake sections. Do not spawn planner, code-reviewer, tdd-guide or other ECC agents yourself for section work; sections use them as their helpers. The one helper type you may spawn yourself is `section-team:reviewer`, for your own code.
- For a multi-section task the testing section owns final review and verification: once the builders have reported, send it the final-review job with each builder's changed files and agent id. Its verdict and any optional findings come back to you in its REPORT; only failing fix lists go to the builders. Do not ask it to send builders a verdict or optional notes. Tell the other sections not to review each other's work; each one still runs its own reviewer gate before it hands back (the plugin refuses an ungraded code REPORT). Never tell a section to skip its gate. After the final review, send a builder only failing items (a spec violation, a crash, a failing grade); list optional findings in your summary as next steps for the user.
- Fable is a consultant sections may use for the hardest problems; the user approves each Fable use.

## New skills
- When the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill, use the `section-team:add-skill` skill.

## Team Board
- Nothing opens by itself. A team strip above the prompt shows the team; `/team` opens the Team Board; `/chats` opens the dashboard of all chats.

## Mode
- This project runs in Max mode (from .team/mode.json).
- Automatic skill installs: off (from SECTION_TEAM_AUTO_INSTALL_SKILLS).
- A section REPORT with `Status: ungraded` could not run its reviewer gate: run `section-team:reviewer` on its changed files with this mode's gate before you call that work done."}}

commands.name: startup-hook-skill
commands.description: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code cloud sessions. Use only when the user asks for a SessionStart hook committed to their repository. Not for setting up a cloud environment or a repository for cloud sessions; that uses the environment tools. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: section-team:add-skill
commands.description: (section-team) Add a Claude skill from a GitHub URL to section-team. Use when the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill or skill repo and wants it added, or runs /section-team:add-skill <url>. Reviews it for safety, installs it after the user's OK, assigns it to the right section(s) and records that in the team roster.

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: advisor
commands.description: Let Claude consult a stronger model at key moments

commands.name: agents
commands.description: (removed) Ask Claude to create/manage subagents, or edit .claude/agents/

commands.name: auto-mode-setup
commands.description: Teach auto mode about your environment, plus optional rule tweaks

commands.description: Configure the auto-compact window size

commands.description: Start a new session with empty context; previous session stays on disk (resumable with /resume)

commands.description: Free up context by summarizing the conversation so far

commands.name: config
commands.description: Set a setting by key

commands.description: List output styles or switch to one

commands.description: Set effort level for model usage

commands.name: heapdump

commands.name: init

commands.name: __remote-workflow
commands.description: Run the workflow script delivered in this session environment (server-launched sessions only)

commands.name: workflow-launch-exec

commands.name: reload-plugins

commands.name: reload-skills
commands.description: Pick up skills added or changed on disk during this session

commands.name: rename
commands.description: Rename the current conversation

commands.name: ultrareview
commands.description: Start a cloud agent that finds and verifies bugs in your branch (~5-15 min, $5-$25 USD) · Runs in a cloud session. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web

commands.name: security-review
commands.description: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

commands.name: usage

commands.name: recap

commands.name: skill-doctor
commands.description: Show which loaded skills are unused and costing context

commands.name: goal
commands.description: Set a goal — keep working until the condition is met

input.content: # Spec — meeting-room booking app (owner: supervisor, verbatim user requirements; FINAL, do not ask questions) Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Node v22. Tests use node:test. Do not use the Fable model. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. ## Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. ## API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. ## Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. ## Page - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. - The page loads the script with a `

# Decisions (supervisor)

- File layout (project root): `server.mjs` (backend), `public/index.html` + `public/app.js` (frontend; server reads them from the folder of server.mjs via `new URL('./public/...', import.meta.url)`, at startup or per request — read failure = 500 `internal error`), `test/*.test.mjs` (testing), `package.json` (backend), `README.md` (docs).
- package.json: `{"type":"module","scripts":{"start":"node server.mjs","test":"node --test test/"}}` — no dependencies.
- Data file layout: `{"nextId": <int>, "bookings": [ {id,room,title,date,start,end}, ... ]}`. Validate fully on load (nextId positive integer > every id; each booking exact keys and valid fields); otherwise `cannot read data file <name>`.
- Saving: write to the data file (writeFile directly to the path; no folder creation). Serialize all mutations through one promise queue so concurrent POSTs behave sequentially. Apply in-memory change only after the write succeeded.
- Spec is in `.team/notes/spec.md` and is final. Where a line can be read two ways, take the stricter reading and note it here.

content.content: # Team notes — one line per note: — — — spec.md — supervisor — full final spec for server, API, booking rules and page — 2026-11-03 decisions.md — supervisor — file layout, data file layout, save/queue strategy — 2026-11-03 ---- # Spec — meeting-room booking app (owner: supervisor, verbatim user requirements; FINAL, do not ask questions) Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Node v22. Tests use node:test. Do not use the Fable model. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. ## Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. ## API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. ## Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. ## Page - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. - The page loads the script with a `

content.content: # Team notes — one line per note: — — — spec.md — supervisor — full final spec for server, API, booking rules and page — 2026-11-03 decisions.md — supervisor — file layout, data file layout, save/queue strategy — 2026-11-03 # Spec — meeting-room booking app (owner: supervisor, verbatim user requirements; FINAL, do not ask questions) Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Node v22. Tests use node:test. Do not use the Fable model. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. ## Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. ## API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. ## Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. ## Page - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. - The page loads the script with a `

# Frontend page (owner: frontend) — 2026-11-03

Files: `public/index.html`, `public/app.js` (classic script, IIFE, runs setup at once).

## Element ids
- `#booking-form` (form, novalidate) holds: `#room` (select, empty in HTML),
  `#title` (input text), `#date` (input date), `#start`, `#end` (input time),
  `#book` (button type=submit, text `Book`). Each field has `<label for>` beside it.
- Outside the form: `#filter-date` (input date, label `Show date`),
  `#show-all` (button type=button, text `Show all`), `#error` (p, role=alert, empty),
  `#booking-list` (ul).
- Script tag `<script src="/app.js"></script>` is the last element in body.

## Requests made by app.js
- `fetch(url, { method: 'GET' })` for `/api/rooms`, `/api/bookings`, `/api/bookings?date=<raw value>`.
- `fetch('/api/bookings', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body })`.
- `fetch('/api/bookings/<id>', { method: 'DELETE' })`; json() is never called on a 204.
- Book / Cancel are re-enabled inside the request helper's `finally`, i.e. right
  when fetch + json() settle, before the outcome is handled.

## Fake-DOM harness: `test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs` (reusable by testing)
- `loadPage({ fetchImpl? })` → `{ document, el(id), calls, flush }`. Runs app.js in
  `node:vm` with only `document` and `fetch` in the global scope.
- Default fetch is controllable: each `calls[i]` has `url`, `options`, `jsonCalls`,
  `resolve(status, body)`, `resolveBadJson(status)`, `reject()`, `resolveWith(response)`.
- Elements: `FakeElement` with value/type/disabled/textContent/childNodes/append/
  replaceChildren/addEventListener, plus test helper `dispatch(type)` returning the
  event (`defaultPrevented`). A `<select>` with no set value reads its first option.
- `listTexts(ul)` → per li `{ text, button: {type,text,disabled}, childCount, nodes }`.
- `flush()` waits a few setImmediate turns.
- Gotcha: objects made inside the vm (e.g. `options.headers`) have another
  `Object.prototype`; compare via JSON round-trip, not `deepStrictEqual`.
EOF
echo "frontend-page.md — frontend — page element ids, request shapes, fake-DOM harness test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs — 2026-11-03" >> INDEX.md
cat >> decisions.md <<'EOF'
- 2026-11-03 · frontend · A list or rooms reply with status 200 whose body lacks the expected array: list → `#error` shows `Request failed.` and the list is kept; rooms → `#room` stays empty. Why: spec is silent; never throw, never replace the list with guessed content.
- 2026-11-03 · frontend · GET requests pass `{ method: 'GET' }` explicitly; any reply with status 204 skips json() (only DELETE expects it; for GET/POST it is then an error status with `Request failed.`). Why: stricter reading of "a reply other than a 204 whose body cannot be read counts as no reply".
- 2026-11-03 · frontend · Book/Cancel re-enable runs in the request helper's `finally`, in the same tick json()/fetch settles. Why: "enabled again as soon as the request settles, before anything else happens".
EOF

Files: `public/index.html`, `public/app.js` (classic script, IIFE, runs setup at once).

## Element ids
- `#booking-form` (form, novalidate) holds: `#room` (select, empty in HTML),
  `#title` (input text), `#date` (input date), `#start`, `#end` (input time),

- Outside the form: `#filter-date` (input date, label `Show date`),
  `#show-all` (button type=button, text `Show all`), `#error` (p, role=alert, empty),
  `#booking-list` (ul).
- `<script src="/app.js"></script>` is the last element in body.

## Requests made by app.js
- `fetch(url, { method: 'GET' })` for `/api/rooms`, `/api/bookings`, `/api/bookings?date=<raw value>`.
- `fetch('/api/bookings', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body })`.
- `fetch('/api/bookings/<id>', { method: 'DELETE' })`; json() is never called on a 204.
- Book / Cancel are re-enabled in the request helper's `finally`, right when
  fetch + json() settle, before the outcome is handled.

## Fake-DOM harness: `test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs` (reusable by testing)
- `loadPage({ fetchImpl? })` -> `{ document, el(id), calls, flush }`. Runs app.js in
  `node:vm` with only `document` and `fetch` in the global scope.

  `resolve(status, body)`, `resolveBadJson(status)`, `reject()`, `resolveWith(response)`.
- `FakeElement`: value/type/disabled/textContent/childNodes/append/replaceChildren/
  addEventListener, plus test helper `dispatch(type)` returning the event

  `dispatch` fires even on disabled elements (like `dispatchEvent`).
- `listTexts(ul)` -> per li `{ text, button: {type,text,disabled}, childCount, nodes }`.
- `flush()` waits a few setImmediate turns.
- Gotcha: objects made inside the vm (e.g. `options.headers`) have another
  `Object.prototype`; compare via a JSON round-trip, not `deepStrictEqual`.
- Frontend's own 28-case check lived outside the repo (/tmp/frontend-check/check.mjs).

# Backend API notes (owner: backend) — 2026-11-03 Implementation: `server.mjs` (single file, Node built-ins only), `package.json`. ## Data file layout `{"nextId": , "bookings": [{"id","room","title","date","start","end"}, ...]}` - Written with `JSON.stringify(store)` (compact) via `fs.promises.writeFile(path)` straight to the DATA_FILE path; no temp file, no folder creation. - Accepted at startup only when: top level is an object with exactly the keys `nextId` and `bookings`; `nextId` safe integer >= 1 and > every id; every booking has exactly the 6 keys, `id` safe integer >= 1 (unique), valid room/date/start/end, `end > start`, title already trimmed and 1-80 UTF-16 units; no two bookings overlap. Anything else (incl. empty file, BOM, `[]`, ENOTDIR, EISDIR, EACCES) -> stderr `cannot read data file ` + exit 1. Only `ENOENT` means "no bookings yet" (nextId 1). - Fixture example for tests: `{"nextId":3,"bookings":[{"id":2,"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}]}` ## Write serialisation - All mutations (POST create, DELETE) go through one promise queue in `createRepository`. Inside the queue: overlap check (rule 10) / id lookup, build the next store, write the file, then swap memory. Write failure -> 500 `internal error`, memory unchanged (nextId too). - Rules 1-9 run before entering the queue; rule 10 runs inside it, so concurrent overlapping POSTs give exactly one 201. ## HTTP details worth knowing for tests - Every request body is read to the end before replying (413/415 included); bytes over 10000 are counted and discarded, the socket is never destroyed early. - Routing uses raw `req.url` split at the first `?`; byte-for-byte path compare. - `http.createServer({ requireHostHeader: false })` so Host-less HTTP/1.1 requests reach routing. - HEAD -> 405 (Node omits the body on HEAD replies, status/headers still sent). - CONNECT is answered on the raw socket: 405 for a known path, 404 otherwise. - Unknown `Expect:` values are routed normally (no automatic 417). - 204 replies carry no body and no Content-Type. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` read `public/index.html` / `public/app.js` per request (relative to server.mjs); read failure -> 500 `internal error`. - Startup failures: invalid PORT -> stderr `invalid PORT ""`; bind failure -> stderr `cannot listen on port

: `; both exit 1. PORT is checked before the data file. - Stdout: only `listening on http://127.0.0.1:\n`. - Smoke script (not a test suite): `.team/backend-smoke/smoke.mjs`.

I graded `server.mjs` (360 lines) and `package.json` against the spec's Server, API, Booking rules and Page-serving sections and against `decisions.md`. There are no project rule files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or `.claude/rules`), so the house rules apply. The smoke script passes all 273 checks. I could not run my own startup checks: permission to run the server directly was denied. So the PORT, DATA_FILE-is-a-directory and port-in-use paths are graded from reading the code.

**Spec conformance (line by line): no deviations found**
- **Startup:** it checks PORT, then reads the data file, then listens, in that order. PORT must be digits only and at most 65535; empty or unset means 3000. Empty DATA_FILE means `bookings.json`, and a relative path is resolved against the working directory. ENOENT means no bookings; any other read error, including a directory, fails startup with `cannot read data file <name>` using the name as given. A failed bind writes one stderr line and exits 1. Stdout gets only the listening line, with the port actually bound.
- **Saving:** every change goes through one promise queue, so requests are handled one at a time. Memory changes only after the write succeeds, and a failed write gives 500 with the next id unchanged. The server creates no folders and never writes at startup.
- **Request body:** the whole body is read before routing, so 404, 405, 413 and 415 replies are all sent after it. Every byte received is counted, and any body over 10000 bytes is thrown away.
- **Routing:** paths are compared byte for byte, cut at the first `?`. The DELETE route matches a non-empty id with no `/`. `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/` give 404. HEAD and OPTIONS on known paths give 405. CONNECT is answered on the raw socket, as the decisions file says.
- **Booking rules 1–10:** checked in order with the exact messages. Content-Type media type trims only spaces and tabs and ignores letter case. The body is decoded with `Buffer.toString('utf8')`, which keeps a byte order mark. Title is trimmed with 1–80 UTF-16 units. Dates run 2000–2099 with February 29 in years divisible by 4. Times run 00:00–23:59, and end must be after start. A 409 reports the earliest-starting overlap, and a booking may start exactly when another ends.
- **Listing:** GET is sorted by date, then start, then room order. `?date` with no value gives 400, and the first value is used when repeated.
- **Other:** the delete id must be a positive integer with no leading zero and is compared as a string. A failed page read gives 500. `package.json` matches the decisions file exactly.

**Minor findings**
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:230-237`: `createBooking` sets `let created` from inside the `mutate` callback. This is a closure side effect, which goes against the immutability rule. Take the new booking from the store that `mutate` resolves with, e.g. `const next = await repo.mutate(...); return next.bookings.at(-1);`.
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:124`: `isValidStore` checks every pair of bookings for overlap, so startup time grows with the square of the booking count. Group by room and date, or sort and compare neighbours.
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:292-305`: if `sendError` itself throws in the `catch` block, the async handler's rejection goes unhandled and the process crashes. This is unlikely to happen. Wrap the reply in its own try/catch that falls back to `res.destroy()`.
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:314`: `handleConnect` builds the JSON error body again by hand instead of reusing a shared helper with `sendJson`/`sendError`.
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:241`: one `HttpError` is created on every call and thrown from two places. Create it where it is thrown, or use a small `bookingNotFound()` factory.

Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — clear layers (validation, store, repository, HTTP helpers, routing, startup) with frozen stores; one closure mutation in createBooking
naming: 9 — descriptive and consistent (matchRoute, findEarliestOverlap, mediaTypeIsJson, MSG table)
duplication: 9 — validators shared between load and POST; small repeat of JSON error-body building in handleConnect
size: 10 — 360-line single file; longest function about 25 lines
errors: 9 — ENOENT told apart from other read errors, bind failures give one stderr line and exit 1, save failures give 500 with no state change, exact spec messages; the handler's catch block has no guard of its own
tests: n/a — written by the testing section
security: 9 — no secrets, no unsafe evaluation, request bodies capped at 10000 bytes, paths not decoded, values sent only as JSON
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, debug code or TODOs; stdout holds only the listening line

- /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:230 drop the `let created` closure mutation; take the created booking from the store `repo.mutate` resolves with
- /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:124 replace the all-pairs overlap check with a grouped or sorted neighbour check
- /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:297 guard the error reply (try/catch falling back to `res.destroy()`) so a throw there cannot become an unhandled rejection
- /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:314 share the JSON error-body building with sendJson/sendError
- /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:241 create the 404 HttpError where it is thrown (or via a small factory), not once ahead of time and shared

# Spec — meeting-room booking app (owner: supervisor, verbatim user requirements; FINAL, do not ask questions) Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Node v22. Tests use node:test. Do not use the Fable model. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. ## Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. ## API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. ## Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. input.content:
# Room bookings

A small meeting-room booking app. It is one HTTP server, `server.mjs`, that:

- serves a JSON API for listing, creating and cancelling bookings of three fixed rooms
  (`Aurora`, `Borealis`, `Cosmos`),
- serves a browser page (`public/index.html` and `public/app.js`) that uses that API,
- keeps every booking in one JSON data file.

## Requirements

- Node.js 22 or later.
- No dependencies: the server and the tests use Node.js built-ins only, so there is
  nothing to `npm install`.

## Usage

Start the server with either command from the project folder:

```sh
npm start
# or
node server.mjs
```

When it is ready it prints one line to stdout:

```
listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

The server only listens on `127.0.0.1` (this machine). That line is the only thing it
ever writes to stdout.

### Configuration

Both settings are environment variables.

| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
|-------------|-----------------|---------|
| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Unset or empty means `3000`. Must be ASCII digits only and at most `65535`. `PORT=0` lets the OS pick a free port; the printed line shows the port actually bound. |
| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the JSON data file. Unset or empty means `bookings.json`. A relative path (the default included) is resolved against the **current working directory**, not the folder of `server.mjs`. |

Examples:

```sh
PORT=8080 npm start
DATA_FILE=/var/lib/rooms/bookings.json node server.mjs
PORT=0 DATA_FILE=tmp/test.json node server.mjs
```

### Startup order and errors

At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening.
If any step fails it writes one line to stderr and exits with code 1 without serving:

| Problem | stderr line |
|---------|-------------|
| `PORT` is not only digits, or is above 65535 | `invalid PORT "<value>"` |
| The data file cannot be read (other than "does not exist"), or its content is not in the layout this server writes (empty, not valid JSON, wrong shape) | `cannot read data file <name>` |
| The port cannot be bound (for example it is already in use) | `cannot listen on port <port>: <error code>` |

`<name>` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when unset or empty).
A data file that does not exist, or whose folder does not exist, is not an error: the
server simply starts with no bookings.

## Using the page

With the server running, open <http://127.0.0.1:3000> in a browser (use your `PORT` if
you changed it). The page lets you:

- book a room: pick the room, enter a title, date, start and end, then press **Book**;
- see the bookings, one per line as `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>`;
- show only one day's bookings with **Show date**, or every booking with **Show all**;
- cancel a booking with its **Cancel** button.

The page does not check the fields itself; any error the server returns (for example
`room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`) is shown above the list. If the server
cannot be reached the page shows `Could not reach the server.`

## API

All API replies with a body are JSON with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.
Errors are `{"error": "<message>"}`.

A booking looks like this:

```json
{ "id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00" }
```

Ids start at 1 and increase by one per new booking. An id is never reused, even after
deletes and restarts.

### Routes

| Method and path | Success | Errors |
|-----------------|---------|--------|
| `GET /api/rooms` | 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}` | |
| `GET /api/bookings` | 200 `{"bookings": [...]}`, sorted by date, then start, then room (in the order above) | |
| `GET /api/bookings?date=YYYY-MM-DD` | 200, only that day's bookings | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
| `POST /api/bookings` | 201 and the new booking | see booking rules below |
| `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` | 204, empty body | 404 `booking not found` |
| `GET /` | 200, the page (`text/html; charset=utf-8`) | |
| `GET /app.js` | 200, the page script (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`) | |

Other replies, for every route:

- Any other path, whatever the method: 404 `not found`. Paths are compared exactly as
  sent (no decoding or case folding), so `/API/rooms`, `/api/bookings/` and
  `/api/bookings/1/` are all 404.
- A known path with a method it does not support (including `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`):
  405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/1` is 405.
- An unexpected failure, including a failed save of the data file: 500 `internal error`.
  Nothing changes and the server keeps running.

Notes:

- The query string is ignored except for `date` on `GET /api/bookings`. `?date` with no
  value counts as an empty (invalid) date; when `date` is repeated, the first one is used.
- `DELETE` returns 404 `booking not found` both when no booking has that id and when
  `<id>` is not a positive whole number without a leading zero (for example `abc` or `01`).

### Example

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'

curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03'

curl -s -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings/1 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'
```

### Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`)

The body must be a JSON object with `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`; other keys
are ignored. Rules are checked in this order and the first failure decides the reply:

| # | Rule | Reply on failure |
|---|------|------------------|
| 1 | `Content-Type` media type is `application/json` (case-insensitive, parameters such as `charset` allowed) | 415 `content type must be application/json` |
| 2 | Body is at most 10000 bytes | 413 `body too large` |
| 3 | Body is a JSON object (not empty, `null`, an array or another value) | 400 `body must be a JSON object` |
| 4 | `room` is exactly `Aurora`, `Borealis` or `Cosmos` (case matters) | 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos` |
| 5 | `title` is a string of 1 to 80 characters after trimming whitespace at both ends; the trimmed title is stored | 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters` |
| 6 | `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31 | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
| 7 | `start` is `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `start must be HH:MM` |
| 8 | `end` is `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `end must be HH:MM` |
| 9 | `end` is later than `start` | 400 `end must be after start` |
| 10 | No overlap with another booking of the same room on the same date (back-to-back is fine) | 409 `room is already booked from <start> to <end>` (the earliest-starting overlapping booking) |

Only `title` is trimmed; other fields must be exact, so ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and
`9:00` are rejected.

Requests sent at the same time are handled as if one after the other: of several
overlapping bookings sent at once, exactly one is created and the others get 409, and
no id is given twice.

## Data file

The data file is JSON in this layout:

```json
{
  "nextId": 3,
  "bookings": [
    { "id": 2, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00" }
  ]
}
```

`nextId` is the id the next booking will get. The server writes the file compactly (one
line); the layout above is spread out only for reading.

Persistence behaviour:

- The file is read once, at startup. After that the server's memory is the truth; edits
  made to the file while the server runs are not noticed (and are overwritten by the
  next save).
- The file is written only when a `POST` creates a booking or a `DELETE` removes one,
  never at startup or for any other request.
- Each change is saved before its reply is sent, so after a restart with the same
  `DATA_FILE` the bookings and the next id are as before.
- The server never creates folders. If a save fails (for example the folder does not
  exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included.
- At startup the file must be exactly in the layout the server writes (exact keys,
  valid fields, unique ids below `nextId`, no overlapping bookings); otherwise the
  server exits with `cannot read data file <name>`.

## Tests

```sh
npm test
```

This runs `node --test test/`, using Node's built-in test runner (`node:test`). Nothing
needs to be installed.

## Project layout

```
server.mjs          HTTP server: API, page serving, data file load and save
public/index.html   the booking page
public/app.js       the page's script (classic script, no build step)
test/               node:test tests
test/helpers/       test helpers (fake-dom.mjs: a minimal DOM to run app.js under Node)
package.json        "start" and "test" scripts; no dependencies
README.md           this file
```
