Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. summary:
## Review: node:test suite for the booking app

**Evidence I checked:** `npm test` passes 390 tests in 4.7 s. I ran near-misses 1, 7, 22 and 35 (overlap `<=`, title `< 80`, list-fetch race, missing "No bookings.") and all four were killed; the unmodified scratch copy exits 0. No `console.log`, `.only` or TODO in `test/`. Every file is 400 lines or fewer and every function is under 50 lines (`runScenario` is about 42).

**What is good:** exact error strings and Content-Type values are asserted with `deepEqual`/`equal`, not prefixes. Boundaries are tested on both sides: 10000/10001 bytes, 80/81 UTF-16 units, emoji 40/41, 65535/65536, 2000-02-29 and 2100. Rule order is tested, including 413 before parsing and invalid end/order before 409. Byte-exact routing is tested over raw sockets, and a pipelined test checks the whole body is read before replying. Restart, save-failure and concurrency tests are strong. The page tests cover overlapping list fetches (cases a–f), whether Book is enabled before the outcome is handled, and an allow-list proxy that is shown to catch bad sources. Temp folders and child processes are always cleaned up in `finally`/`after`.

### Missing spec coverage (spec line → missing test)
1. **spec:12 "not data in the layout this server writes"** (and decisions:5/11): only a missing key and an extra key are tested. There are no cases for:
   - `nextId` ≤ the largest id, e.g. `{"nextId":1,"bookings":[{id:2,…}]}`
   - duplicate ids
   - `nextId` 0, 1.5 or `"3"`
   - a non-integer id
   - a stored booking with an invalid date or time
   - an untrimmed stored title
   - overlapping stored bookings

   A loader that accepts `nextId:1` next to id 2 hands out a duplicate id and passes every current test.
2. **spec:15 "Any other unexpected failure … 500 `internal error` … keeps running"** (decisions:3: public file read failure = 500): no test. Copy `server.mjs` into a temp folder without `public/`, then check that `GET /` and `GET /app.js` give 500 `{"error":"internal error"}` with the JSON Content-Type, and that `/api/rooms` still answers 200.
3. **spec:10 "This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout"**: stdout is checked only after a few successful GETs (`startup.test.mjs:96-103`). After the 500 save failures in `persistence.test.mjs:101-136`, neither stdout nor stderr is checked. A server that runs `console.log(err)` on 500 passes.
4. **spec:57 "A reply other than a 204 whose body cannot be read … counts as no reply"** for DELETE: there is no Cancel test with `resolveBadJson(404)` expecting `Could not reach the server.` and no list refetch. A version that treats this as `Request failed.` and refetches passes.
5. **spec:57 success status per method** for DELETE: nothing checks that DELETE answered with 200 (not 204) is an error status. Submit has the matching test (`page-actions.test.mjs:134`); Cancel does not.
6. **spec:9 unset `PORT` means 3000**: only `PORT=''` gets as far as listening (`startup.test.mjs:157`). Unset `PORT` is only checked on the port-in-use path.

### Quality issues
- **Silently passing tests:**
  - `startup.test.mjs:121-125`: a bare `catch { return; }` swallows every error, not just EADDRINUSE, and the test reports a pass.
  - `startup.test.mjs:156`: `if (!holder) return;` also passes silently.
  - Both should use `t.skip(...)`.
- **Weak assertion:** `request-body.test.mjs:231` is `raw.includes(ROOMS_JSON.slice(1,-1)) || raw.includes('"rooms"')`. The second half makes the first pointless. It should parse the second reply's body and `deepEqual` it to the rooms object.
- **Brittle against decisions:15:**
  - `page-actions.test.mjs:187` and `:275` only notice the list refetch when `call.options?.method === 'GET'`.
  - A valid `app.js` that calls `fetch(url)` with no options gives `seen = []`, so the test fails.
  - Both should use the existing `methodOf(call) === 'GET'`.
- **Duplication:**
  - `uniqueDate` is identical in `booking-rules.test.mjs:15-23` and `request-body.test.mjs:10-17`.
  - `withTemp` is in both `startup.test.mjs:16` and `persistence.test.mjs:12`.
  - `expectError` is repeated in `routing:31`, `booking-rules:29` and `request-body:65`.
  - `JSON_TYPE` is defined in 4 files.
  - `NO_REPLY`, `FAILED` and `methodOf` appear in both `page-load-list:5-8` and `page-actions:5-12`.
  - `page-script-api.test.mjs:73-76` (SPECS) and `:117` (flush) copy `fake-dom.mjs`.
  - The "enabled before #error is set" setter spy appears twice (`page-actions:199-213`, `:284-297`).
- **Readability:**
  - `startup.test.mjs:299-321`: passing an `undefined` status to mean "skip this call" is a hack.
  - `booking-rules.test.mjs:72,80-81`: the titles contain invisible U+3000, U+00A0 and U+FEFF characters. The "inner NBSP" case is correct, but it looks identical to the line above it.
  - `routing.test.mjs:140` ignores the POST result.

Against the stricter gate you set (overall at least 9, no item under 7), this suite fails: overall is 8 and duplication is 6.

## GRADE
Overall: 8/10
Verdict: fail
structure: 8 — helpers are well separated, but page-actions hooks depend on `options.method` and fireNonMutating uses an `undefined`-status skip hack
naming: 8 — mostly clear, with some terse names (`mk`, `B1`/`X`/`Y`, `before_`/`after_`) and invisible Unicode in fixtures
duplication: 6 — uniqueDate, withTemp, expectError, JSON_TYPE, NO_REPLY/FAILED/methodOf, SPECS/flush and the textContent spy are copied across files
size: 9 — all files ≤ 348 lines, all functions < 50 lines
errors: 7 — startup.test.mjs:123 bare catch swallows every error and the test passes; :156 is a silent return instead of t.skip
tests: 8 — exact values, both-side boundaries, near-misses killed and deterministic cleanup, but gaps in data-file validation, the 500 unexpected-failure path, stdout after errors, DELETE bad-JSON and non-204 handling, plus one OR-weakened assertion
security: 10 — no secrets; temp folders are isolated and child processes get a stripped env

summary:
I found no spec violations in the code. One required fix is in the README: it states the wrong test command. The verdict is a pass.

`npm test` gave 414 passing out of 414. I couldn't run my own probes, because Bash only allows the test command here. So I checked startup failures by reading the code and confirming the tests in `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/startup.test.mjs` cover them: bad PORT values, port in use, a data path that is a directory, a file in the middle of the path, and a byte order mark (BOM) at the start of the file.

## (A) Must fix

1. **README gives the wrong test command.** `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/README.md:198` says `This runs node --test test/`. The script in `package.json` is `node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"`. Per the decisions file, `node --test test/` fails on Node 22, so anyone following the README gets a failing run.

### Spec lines checked against the code, all as specified
- **Startup:** PORT is checked first, then the data file is read, then the server listens. PORT must be ASCII digits only and at most 65535, using a regex with no multiline flag, so trailing newlines and Arabic-Indic digits are rejected. An unset or empty PORT means 3000. If the port can't be bound, the server writes one line and exits 1. The PORT error line runs the value through `JSON.stringify`, so a PORT containing a newline still gives one line. stdout gets only the `listening on` line, with the port actually bound.
- **Data file:** an unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`, and relative paths resolve against the current working directory. ENOENT means no bookings yet. Any other read error, or content not in the exact written layout, gives `cannot read data file <name as given>`. The file is written only on a successful POST or DELETE, and memory changes only after the write succeeds (lines 159-163). All changes go through one queue, so overlapping bookings sent at once give exactly one 201 and the rest 409.
- **Request body:** the whole body is read before any reply (line 293), so 413 and 415 replies arrive. The content type is checked before the size. The size counts the bytes actually received. A BOM is kept, because `Buffer#toString` does not strip it.
- **Routing:** paths are compared raw. `/api/bookings/<id>` matches only when the id is non-empty and has no `/`. The DELETE id must match `^[1-9][0-9]*$` and is compared as a string. HEAD, OPTIONS and CONNECT get 405 or 404. The `?date` filter uses `has`/`get`. The 204 reply has no body.
- **Booking rules 1-10:** they run in order. The title uses `trim` and is limited by UTF-16 length. Date and time checks use ASCII digits with leap years every 4 years. The overlap check uses strict `<` on both sides, and the 409 names the overlapping booking that starts earliest.

# Room bookings

A small meeting-room booking app. It is one HTTP server, `server.mjs`, that:

- serves a JSON API for listing, creating and cancelling bookings of three fixed rooms
  (`Aurora`, `Borealis`, `Cosmos`),
- serves a browser page (`public/index.html` and `public/app.js`) that uses that API,
- keeps every booking in one JSON data file.

## Requirements

- Node.js 22 or later.
- No dependencies: the server and the tests use Node.js built-ins only, so there is
  nothing to `npm install`.

## Usage

Start the server with either command from the project folder:

```sh
npm start
# or
node server.mjs
```

When it is ready it prints one line to stdout:

```
listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

The server only listens on `127.0.0.1` (this machine). That line is the only thing it
ever writes to stdout.

### Configuration

Both settings are environment variables.

| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
|-------------|-----------------|---------|
| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Unset or empty means `3000`. Must be ASCII digits only and at most `65535`. `PORT=0` lets the OS pick a free port; the printed line shows the port actually bound. |
| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the JSON data file. Unset or empty means `bookings.json`. A relative path (the default included) is resolved against the **current working directory**, not the folder of `server.mjs`. |

Examples:

```sh
PORT=8080 npm start
DATA_FILE=/var/lib/rooms/bookings.json node server.mjs
PORT=0 DATA_FILE=tmp/test.json node server.mjs
```

### Startup order and errors

At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening.
If any step fails it writes one line to stderr and exits with code 1 without serving:

| Problem | stderr line |
|---------|-------------|
| `PORT` is not only digits, or is above 65535 | `invalid PORT "<value>"` |
| The data file cannot be read (other than "does not exist"), or its content is not in the layout this server writes (empty, not valid JSON, wrong shape) | `cannot read data file <name>` |
| The port cannot be bound (for example it is already in use) | `cannot listen on port <port>: <error code>` |

`<name>` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when unset or empty).
A data file that does not exist, or whose folder does not exist, is not an error: the
server simply starts with no bookings.

## Using the page

With the server running, open <http://127.0.0.1:3000> in a browser (use your `PORT` if
you changed it). The page lets you:

- book a room: pick the room, enter a title, date, start and end, then press **Book**;
- see the bookings, one per line as `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>`;
- show only one day's bookings with **Show date**, or every booking with **Show all**;
- cancel a booking with its **Cancel** button.

The page does not check the fields itself; any error the server returns (for example
`room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`) is shown above the list. If the server
cannot be reached the page shows `Could not reach the server.`

## API

All API replies with a body are JSON with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.
Errors are `{"error": "<message>"}`.

A booking looks like this:

```json
{ "id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00" }
```

Ids start at 1 and increase by one per new booking. An id is never reused, even after
deletes and restarts.

### Routes

| Method and path | Success | Errors |
|-----------------|---------|--------|
| `GET /api/rooms` | 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}` | |
| `GET /api/bookings` | 200 `{"bookings": [...]}`, sorted by date, then start, then room (in the order above) | |
| `GET /api/bookings?date=YYYY-MM-DD` | 200, only that day's bookings | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
| `POST /api/bookings` | 201 and the new booking | see booking rules below |
| `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` | 204, empty body | 404 `booking not found` |
| `GET /` | 200, the page (`text/html; charset=utf-8`) | |
| `GET /app.js` | 200, the page script (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`) | |

Other replies, for every route:

- Any other path, whatever the method: 404 `not found`. Paths are compared exactly as
  sent (no decoding or case folding), so `/API/rooms`, `/api/bookings/` and
  `/api/bookings/1/` are all 404.
- A known path with a method it does not support (including `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`):
  405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/1` is 405.
- An unexpected failure, including a failed save of the data file: 500 `internal error`.
  Nothing changes and the server keeps running.

Notes:

- The query string is ignored except for `date` on `GET /api/bookings`. `?date` with no
  value counts as an empty (invalid) date; when `date` is repeated, the first one is used.
- `DELETE` returns 404 `booking not found` both when no booking has that id and when
  `<id>` is not a positive whole number without a leading zero (for example `abc` or `01`).

### Example

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'

curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03'

curl -s -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings/1 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'
```

### Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`)

The body must be a JSON object with `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`; other keys
are ignored. Rules are checked in this order and the first failure decides the reply:

| # | Rule | Reply on failure |
|---|------|------------------|
| 1 | `Content-Type` media type is `application/json` (case-insensitive, parameters such as `charset` allowed) | 415 `content type must be application/json` |
| 2 | Body is at most 10000 bytes | 413 `body too large` |
| 3 | Body is a JSON object (not empty, `null`, an array or another value) | 400 `body must be a JSON object` |
| 4 | `room` is exactly `Aurora`, `Borealis` or `Cosmos` (case matters) | 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos` |
| 5 | `title` is a string of 1 to 80 characters after trimming whitespace at both ends; the trimmed title is stored | 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters` |
| 6 | `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31 | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
| 7 | `start` is `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `start must be HH:MM` |
| 8 | `end` is `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `end must be HH:MM` |
| 9 | `end` is later than `start` | 400 `end must be after start` |
| 10 | No overlap with another booking of the same room on the same date (back-to-back is fine) | 409 `room is already booked from <start> to <end>` (the earliest-starting overlapping booking) |

Only `title` is trimmed; other fields must be exact, so ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and
`9:00` are rejected.

Requests sent at the same time are handled as if one after the other: of several
overlapping bookings sent at once, exactly one is created and the others get 409, and
no id is given twice.

## Data file

The data file is JSON in this layout:

```json
{
  "nextId": 3,
  "bookings": [
    { "id": 2, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00" }
  ]
}
```

`nextId` is the id the next booking will get. The server writes the file compactly (one
line); the layout above is spread out only for reading.

Persistence behaviour:

- The file is read once, at startup. After that the server's memory is the truth; edits
  made to the file while the server runs are not noticed (and are overwritten by the
  next save).
- The file is written only when a `POST` creates a booking or a `DELETE` removes one,
  never at startup or for any other request.
- Each change is saved before its reply is sent, so after a restart with the same
  `DATA_FILE` the bookings and the next id are as before.
- The server never creates folders. If a save fails (for example the folder does not
  exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included.
- At startup the file must be exactly in the layout the server writes (exact keys,
  valid fields, unique ids below `nextId`, no overlapping bookings); otherwise the
  server exits with `cannot read data file <name>`.

## Tests

```sh
npm test
```

This runs `node --test test/`, using Node's built-in test runner (`node:test`). Nothing
needs to be installed.

## Project layout

```
server.mjs          HTTP server: API, page serving, data file load and save
public/index.html   the booking page
public/app.js       the page's script (classic script, no build step)
test/               node:test tests
test/helpers/       test helpers (fake-dom.mjs: a minimal DOM to run app.js under Node)
package.json        "start" and "test" scripts; no dependencies
README.md           this file
```

The meeting-room booking app is built and the project's own tests pass: `npm test` ran 414 tests with 0 failures. The security review didn't run as planned, so I did a smaller security check myself (below).

**What's there**
- **`server.mjs`:** the JSON API and the browser page, with bookings saved to one data file. It uses only Node built-ins.
- **`public/index.html` and `public/app.js`:** the booking page and its script. The script uses only the browser APIs the spec allows.
- **`test/`:** 11 test files covering the server, the API and the page. To check that the tests catch real bugs, 42 copies of the code were made, each with one plausible bug. The suite fails on every one of them.
- **`package.json` and `README.md`:** the start and test scripts, and usage instructions.

**Per section**

- ✅ **Frontend** built the page and its script. Code review: 9/10.

- ❌ **Security** stopped with an error twice. Its review step compares against a git remote, and this repo has none.
  - Instead I ran the server and tried crafted requests: special JSON keys, odd booking ids, a request cut off mid-body, a malformed request line and a 50 KB body.
  - Each got the correct reply and the server stayed up.

**Decisions where the spec allowed more than one reading** (all recorded in `.team/notes/decisions.md`):
- The data file is `{"nextId", "bookings"}`, and the server refuses at startup to load any file that isn't exactly that layout.
- Saves happen one at a time, so of several overlapping bookings sent at once, only one is created.
- If a file sits where a folder in the data file's path should be, the server stops at startup, the same as for a directory.

- `fetch(url, { method: 'GET' })` for `/api/rooms`, `/api/bookings`, `/api/bookings?date=<raw value>`.
- `fetch('/api/bookings', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body })`.
- `fetch('/api/bookings/<id>', { method: 'DELETE' })`; json() is never called on a 204.
- Book / Cancel are re-enabled inside the request helper's `finally`, i.e. right
  when fetch + json() settle, before the outcome is handled.

## Fake-DOM harness: `test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs` (reusable by testing)
- `loadPage({ fetchImpl? })` → `{ document, el(id), calls, flush }`. Runs app.js in
  `node:vm` with only `document` and `fetch` in the global scope.
- Default fetch is controllable: each `calls[i]` has `url`, `options`, `jsonCalls`,
  `resolve(status, body)`, `resolveBadJson(status)`, `reject()`, `resolveWith(response)`.
- Elements: `FakeElement` with value/type/disabled/textContent/childNodes/append/
  replaceChildren/addEventListener, plus test helper `dispatch(type)` returning the
  event (`defaultPrevented`). A `<select>` with no set value reads its first option.
- `listTexts(ul)` → per li `{ text, button: {type,text,disabled}, childCount, nodes }`.
- `flush()` waits a few setImmediate turns.
- Gotcha: objects made inside the vm (e.g. `options.headers`) have another
  `Object.prototype`; compare via JSON round-trip, not `deepStrictEqual`.

result:
The meeting-room booking app is built and the project's own tests pass: `npm test` ran 414 tests with 0 failures. The security review didn't run as planned, so I did a smaller security check myself (below).

**What's there**
- **`server.mjs`:** the JSON API and the browser page, with bookings saved to one data file. It uses only Node built-ins.
- **`public/index.html` and `public/app.js`:** the booking page and its script. The script uses only the browser APIs the spec allows.
- **`test/`:** 11 test files covering the server, the API and the page. To check that the tests catch real bugs, 42 copies of the code were made, each with one plausible bug. The suite fails on every one of them.
- **`package.json` and `README.md`:** the start and test scripts, and usage instructions.

**Per section**
- ✅ **Backend** built the server and `package.json`. Code review: 9/10.
- ✅ **Frontend** built the page and its script. Code review: 9/10.
- ✅ **Testing** wrote the suite and found no spec violations in its final review. Code review: 9/10.
  - It changed the test script to `node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"`, because on Node 22 `node --test test/` fails.
  - I updated the README to match.
- ✅ **Docs** wrote the README.
- ❌ **Security** stopped with an error twice. Its review step compares against a git remote, and this repo has none.
  - Instead I ran the server and tried crafted requests: special JSON keys, odd booking ids, a request cut off mid-body, a malformed request line and a 50 KB body.
  - Each got the correct reply and the server stayed up.
  - The page and its script use no unsafe HTML insertion and contain no `http://` or `https://`.

**Decisions where the spec allowed more than one reading** (all recorded in `.team/notes/decisions.md`):
- The data file is `{"nextId", "bookings"}`, and the server refuses at startup to load any file that isn't exactly that layout.
- Saves happen one at a time, so of several overlapping bookings sent at once, only one is created.
- If a file sits where a folder in the data file's path should be, the server stops at startup, the same as for a directory.

**Next steps (optional)**
- Save the data file by writing a temporary file and renaming it over the original, so a crash mid-write can't corrupt it.
- A `node server.mjs` process left over from the backend's manual checks may still be running (pid 9751). I couldn't check it without your approval.
